_about: Suggested Claude model and effort per phase. These are suggestions from reading what each phase asks for, not benchmarks: edit them freely. Models are Claude Code's aliases (they follow the newest model of that name); which ones you can use depends on your account. Effort is Claude Code's --effort level: low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Higher effort is slower and uses more of your usage.

research.why: Judging sources and making a go, pivot or stop call is reasoning-heavy and cheap to get wrong now, expensive later.

plan.why: Architecture, tenancy and security choices here are the hardest to undo once code exists.

foundation.why: Auth, tenant scoping and migrations must be right; with a clear plan, medium effort is usually enough.

product.why: UI work is many small build-and-look steps where speed helps; the browser check catches mistakes.

ship.why: CI, environments and rollbacks are routine once decided; the gates verify the result.

harden.why: A security review that misses something is worse than a slow one; use the strongest setting you have.

operate.why: Logging, health checks and alerts are well-trodden patterns.

launch.why: Copy, legal pages and video briefs benefit from iteration more than from deep reasoning.

scale.why: Finding a real bottleneck from measurements takes careful reasoning, but the build steps are small.

tasks.task: A small copy or style tweak
tasks.why: Fast and cheap; nothing to reason about.

tasks.task: Reading a long document or PDF
